title: Effect of surface acidity of activated carbon on hydrogen storage
material_description: 1 | commercial activated carbon no. 1 of Table 1 (printed "1)"), BET N2 1012 m2/gm, oxygen content 12.8%; soxhlet water-washed 5 h and oven-dried at 393 K
purification_method: washed with distilled water in a soxhlet extraction apparatus for 5 hours; oven dried at 393 K
notes: archive: HYC-0089_fig1_sample1.json. Digitized 0.9553 atm, 12.1791 g H2/kg carbon (g/kg = mg/g); pressure_bar = atm x 1.01325; uptake_wt_pct = W1 = 0.1 x g/kg. Marker = plotted numeral "1" (1 of 10 markers), located by template matching and digitized with digitize_figure.py markers mode. Table 1 (main-2.png, p. 220): surface area 1012 m2/gm (Nitrogen BET, Quantasorb Quantachrome; BET range not stated), oxygen content 12.8% (total oxygen by difference after Micro-Analysis Inc. elemental C, H, N and ash at 773 K). Gravimetric, Cahn 1000 high pressure recording electrobalance, 78 K. Buoyancy corrections stated: blank runs for the pyrex holder; sample volume from manufacturer-supplied skeletal density (1.8-2.2 gm/ml for all samples, not stored) with H2 density from the ideal gas law; "buoyancy corrections for the adsorbed phase will not be applied". The paper describes the gravimetric observed amount as the difference with respect to an equivalent amount of gas in the same volume but never names a basis (the phrase "total hydrogen adsorbed" appears once, meaning overall amount vs per unit area), so uptake_type unspecified, basis_stated false, basis_inferred excess by the gravimetric-with-buoyancy-correction default. Reproducibility: "Selected replicate experiments ... maximum error was less than 2%" (relative, not wt%; uncertainty_wt_pct left empty). Degas printed: evacuated to 10^-8 Pa at 393 K for 18 hours, then flowing helium 15 minutes and re-evacuated. Sample mass printed as a range, 100-200 mgms (not stored). H2 99.9999% (ultra-high purity), deoxo unit and LN2 trap. Pressure axis in atm; gauges MKS Baratron 222B 0-1000 Torr and Data Instrument EA 0-2000 psig; plotted pressure not called gauge, treated as absolute. Commercial carbon; manufacturer and product not named.
